Epiphany (Three Kings Day)

Epiphany Celebration: Welcoming the Magi at Home

Celebrate the Epiphany by honoring the arrival of the Three Kings with meaningful traditions, joyful activities, and delicious festive foods that bring family and friends together.

  1. Morning

    Bless Your Doorway with Chalk

    Begin the day by blessing your home's entrance with chalk, marking the initials of the Three Kings and the year to invite good fortune and protection throughout the year.

  2. Late Morning

    Prepare a Festive Stew

    Slowly simmer a traditional stew to enjoy later at the feast; this hearty dish reflects warmth and togetherness during the celebration.

    Recipes: Traditional Epiphany Beef Stew

  3. Noon

    Stage a Three Kings Pageant

    Engage family members in a lively reenactment of the Magi’s journey, complete with costumes and a camel prop, to bring the story of Epiphany to life.

  4. Afternoon

    Bake a Rosca de Reyes or King Cake

    Bake a traditional Rosca de Reyes or King Cake, symbolizing the circular journey of the Magi and the unity of family and friends.

    Recipes: Rosca De Reyes · King Cake

  5. Late Afternoon

    Enjoy Hot Chocolate and Cake

    Gather to sip rich, warming hot chocolate alongside slices of your freshly baked cake, savoring the flavors that celebrate the season.

    Recipes: Traditional Spanish Hot Chocolate · King Cake · Rosca De Reyes

  6. Evening

    Share the Festive Stew Dinner

    Conclude the day with a shared meal of the slow-simmered stew, fostering community and gratitude as you reflect on the festival’s meaning.

    Recipes: Traditional Epiphany Beef Stew

  7. Night

    Exchange Gifts and Reflect

    End the celebration by exchanging gifts as children receive surprises from Los Reyes Magos or La Befana, honoring the tradition of generosity and hope.

Close the day with joy and gratitude, carrying the spirit of revelation and unity into the year ahead.
